title: Wringer evidence event
description: One line of evidence.jsonl. The file is append-only, one JSON object per line, in the order things happened. This schema describes a single line, not the file. Every event carries `type` and `ts`; the rest depends on `type`. Absent optional keys are meaningful — see each description.

ts.description: Local ISO-8601 with UTC offset, millisecond precision. Fine enough to order two fast gates, coarse enough to stay readable.

prev_hash.description: sha256 of the previous whole line in this ledger, or 64 zeros for the first. Every event links to the one before it, so altering or removing a line breaks every hash after it. Tamper-EVIDENCE, not tamper-proofing: anyone who can write the file can rewrite the chain, but silent edits become detectable. Written now; `wring attest` / `wring audit` are the slice that verifies it.

repo.description: The repo directory's name, not a path or a URL.

sha.description: Full HEAD SHA, or null when git could not be read.

oneOf.title: git.status
oneOf.description: Written before the bundle directory exists, so a run never reports its own evidence as an untracked change.

changed_files.description: Repo-relative paths git already tracks. A patch can describe these; diff.patch does.

untracked.description: Repo-relative paths git has never seen. PRESENT ONLY when non-empty, so the common case keeps the spec's shape. Absent means none, not unknown.

oneOf.title: gate.finished
oneOf.description: A gate.started with no matching gate.finished means the run was interrupted while that gate was running. No verdict is invented for it.

log.description: Bundle-relative path to the log a reader is being sent to. PRESENT ONLY for a failing gate — it is a pointer, not an inventory; every gate's logs are on disk and linked from summary.md.

truncated.description: PRESENT ONLY when true. Absent means the logs are whole.

failed_gate.description: PRESENT ONLY when a required gate failed.
